ana: Heads-up — ran a full trace backtest (production traces -> anonymized -> playback) and we have a non-obvious perf delta vs the golden run. Small note thread to track clues and next steps. marcus: Can you paste the top-level numbers? latency / p95 / token/sec? sara: +1, and which model/kernel combo did you force for the golden? ana: sorry typo — ana. Numbers: golden: p50=48ms p95=112ms tokens/sec=1890. Backtest run: p50=51ms p95=138ms tokens/sec=1720. Diff seems concentrated at batch sizes 1-4. lee: interesting — is kernel selection flipping between matmul_v1 and matmul_v2 or similar? small seq-length differences can trigger different kernel paths. ana: (ana) I dug into the profiler; at sequence length boundary 256 we see matmul_v2 chosen for many steps in the backtest, whereas the golden used the older matmul_v1 kernel for identical model/weights. Kernel choice log: ``` [2026-03-01T10:12:34Z] seq=255 kernel=matmul_v1 [2026-03-01T10:12:34Z] seq=256 kernel=matmul_v2 ``` marcus: Wait — why would seq change? traces were anonymized — did we replace long tokens with a single token that shifted tokenization? sara: Exactly this. Our anonymizer compresses email/urls to

which reduces token count and slightly changes offsets. That can push a lot of requests across the 256 boundary. lee: That explains both kernel flip and KV cache warmup differences. If prefixes are shrunk, kv-cache hit rates drop, causing extra compute. Did you check KV hit curves? ana: yes — KV warmup graph shows 40% fewer cached entries in first 300ms. I attached a small inline snippet of the sampling diff we saw: ``` trace_id: X orig_tokens: 1 23 456 789 1023 2048 ... (len=278) anon_tokens: 1 23 456

2048 ... (len=248) ``` perf-bot: Regression alert created: PERF-3241 (severity: medium) — attaching perf logs. marcus: Two-pronged action: (1) change anonymizer to preserve tokenization length/profile (or at least token-type placeholders that keep token counts), (2) make playback/backtest apples-to-apples by forcing kernel selection and forcing identical batching heuristics. sara: For (1) we can replace long spans with token-length-preserving placeholders, e.g., replace "long_text" -> "" so tokenizer output keeps same length. That keeps seq distribution intact. lee: For (2) we already have env overrides: `FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_v1` and `BATCH_HEURISTICS=legacy` for the harness. We should run a 2x test: (A) backtest with current anonymizer + no force, (B) backtest with length-preserving anonymizer + no force, (C) length-preserving anonymizer + forced kernel+heuristics. Compare all three. ana: I've got a quick command combo for the harness: ``` ./tools/trace_backtest \ --trace=anon_trace.json \ --model=redwood/turbo-1 \ --force-kernel=$FORCE_KERNEL \ --batch-config=./configs/legacy_batch.json \ --out=run.out ``` lee: For parity checks, note we shouldn't rely on fp bitwise equal for perf parity. Use token-id sequence equality or logprob delta threshold. Example comparator: ``` ./compare_tokens --gold gold.tokens --run run.tokens --mode=exact # fallback: ./compare_tokens --gold gold.tokens --run run.tokens --mode=approx --tol=1e-3 ``` marcus: Also add a stratified sampling tweak for synthetic testsets so we don't over-index short/long sequences. Proposed script: ``` python tools/strat_sample.py \ --trace trace.json \ --buckets 0-32,33-128,129-512 \ --ratios 0.4,0.4,0.2 \ --out sample.json ``` sara: Quick note on nondeterminism: some kernels reorder reductions and give tiny fp diffs that still change softmax order for near-equal logits. We'll need the comparator's approx mode and also a per-token-stability metric (how often top-1 changes). ana: I'll run the three test variants tomorrow morning (A/B/C), capture kernel logs, kv-hit curves, and token-delta summaries. Expect ~2-3 hours per run. Posting results to this thread. lee: If length-preserving anonymizer fixes it, we should update anonymization pipeline and re-run a historical backtest before merging. marcus: Assigning owners: ana -> run tests + upload artifacts; sara -> prototype length-preserving anonymizer; lee -> add forced-kernel harness flag to the orchestrator; I'll handle the regression ticket and perf dashboards. ana: ack. Also adding a small note: we should include a lightweight sanity-check step in the ingest pipeline that computes token-length histograms pre/post anonymization and fails if distributions diverge >5%. sara: love that. I'll prototype a check. perf-bot: build 7890 completed; artifacts uploaded to PERF-3241. marcus: Thanks all. Keep this thread for results. :thumbsup:
